[quote=shahzada;58246203][b]Question of the Day #24:[/b]

How does your nation celebrate its culture?

[i]This is an automated message.[/i][/quote]

Many small, local celebrations happen all across the country every year, attracting tourists while also exemplifying the culture of the ULR.
Many foods, historical reenactments, and museum displays can be seen in these towns during such celebrations. Some native foods and drinks include:
- Chi-pan: Breaded and baked balls of meat, normally consisting of chicken or pork
- Bena: A drink consisting of fresh coconut water mixed with the juice of wild berries, normally served in the shell of the coconut.
- Yokar: A dish consisting of Pirari corn (a version of corn with slightly tougher, larger kernels), chicken meat, egg, and various spices, along with mushrooms. Served in a bowl as a mix, it's a favorite of both native and tourist for lunch or dinner.

[quote=shahzada;58246203][b]Question of the Day #24:[/b]

How does your nation celebrate its culture?

[i]This is an automated message.[/i][/quote]

1.Lumenfest
Celebrated on the longest day of the year, this festival includes parades, music, dancing, and communal feasts, where people gather to celebrate the warmth and light of summer. Artisans showcase their crafts, and local delicacies are shared among the community.
2.Nachtzeit
The longest night of the year is marked with intimate gatherings, candlelight ceremonies, and storytelling sessions. Families come together to share traditions and listen to ancient tales, emphasizing the importance of unity and reflection during this time.
3.Ewigkeitfest
This festival commemorates 2500 years of Ekpatanos rich history. During this grand celebration, military forces parade through the main streets of the capital cities, Apadana and Aurelia, wearing ancient uniforms and demonstrating their evolution. This showcases the development of the army from ancient times to the present, reflecting the nations heritage and strength.
